G-F031.trick: An enzyme digs a tunnel through the hill: same start and end, easier path (lower activation energy).
G-F031.tip: Enzymes speed reactions by lowering activation energy. They don't change how much energy the reaction releases overall.

G-F032.trick: Lock and key: an inhibitor is a wrong key jammed in the lock, so the right key can't fit.
G-F032.tip: Selective effects come from shape fit at the active site. Specific shape = specific substrate.

G-F033.trick: OIL RIG: Oxidation Is Loss, Reduction Is Gain (of electrons).
G-F033.tip: Don't let the word "oxidation" fool you into thinking oxygen must be added. Focus on electrons.

G-F034.tip: "Net" means subtract what was invested. Always check whether a question asks gross or net yield.

G-F035.trick: Citric acid (Krebs) cycle: acetyl (2C) + oxaloacetate (4C) = citrate (6C), and the 4C comes back around.
G-F035.tip: If a cycle in the mitochondrial matrix regenerates its starting molecule, it is the Krebs/citric acid cycle.

G-F036.trick: Proton gradient = water behind a dam. A leak lets water bypass the turbine (ATP synthase): less power.
G-F036.tip: Electron transport builds the gradient; ATP synthase uses it. Break the gradient and ATP output falls.

G-F037.trick: DE-amination = remove the AMINE (nitrogen) tag, then burn the carbon body.
G-F037.tip: Proteins become fuel only after deamination. The removed nitrogen becomes ammonia, then urea.

G-F038.trick: Lagging strand = building a fence walking backward: short pieces (Okazaki fragments) glued by ligase.
G-F038.tip: DNA polymerase only builds 5′→3′. That one rule explains the leading strand and the lagging-strand fragments.

G-F039.trick: Stop codon = the period at the end of the sentence. UAA, UAG, UGA: "U Are Away, U Are Gone, U Go Away".
G-F039.tip: Stop codons don't code an amino acid. They bring release factors that free the finished chain.

G-F040.trick: The code has synonyms: several codons "spell" the same amino acid, like color and colour.
G-F040.tip: A silent mutation changes DNA but not the protein. This works because the code is redundant (degenerate).

C-ch4-enzymes.trick: SUBSTRATE = the SUBJECT the enzyme works on. Enzyme + substrate → products.
C-ch4-enzymes.tip: The substrate binds the active site. The enzyme comes out unchanged and can be reused.
C-ch4-enzymes.why: A substrate is the reactant an enzyme acts on: it binds the enzyme's active site and is converted into products. A coenzyme is an organic helper molecule (often made from a vitamin), and the enzyme itself comes out unchanged.

C-ch4-atp.trick: OIL RIG: Oxidation Is Loss of electrons.
C-ch4-atp.tip: When a molecule is oxidized, another must be reduced. They always happen as a pair (redox).
C-ch4-atp.why: Oxidation is the loss of electrons; reduction is the gain of electrons, and the two always happen together. Phosphorylation adds a phosphate group, and hydrolysis splits a bond using water.

C-ch4-glycolysis.trick: GLYCO-LYSIS = sugar-splitting. 1 glucose → 2 pyruvate, in the cytosol, no oxygen needed.
C-ch4-glycolysis.tip: Glycolysis happens in the cytoplasm and doesn't need oxygen. Krebs and the electron transport chain are in the mitochondria.
C-ch4-glycolysis.why: Glycolysis splits one glucose into two pyruvate in the cytosol, for a net 2 ATP and 2 NADH, without needing oxygen. The Krebs cycle runs in the mitochondrial matrix, glycogenesis builds glycogen, and beta-oxidation breaks down fatty acids.

C-ch4-aerobic.trick: Krebs cycle = the mitochondrial merry-go-round that strips electrons off acetyl groups.
C-ch4-aerobic.tip: Location matters: Krebs is in the matrix; the electron transport chain is on the inner membrane.
C-ch4-aerobic.why: The Krebs (citric acid) cycle in the mitochondrial matrix oxidizes acetyl groups, releasing CO₂ and loading NADH and FADH₂, and regenerates oxaloacetate to start again. Glycolysis happens in the cytosol, the electron transport chain sits on the inner membrane, and beta-oxidation breaks fatty acids into acetyl units.

C-ch4-fuels.trick: BETA-oxidation chops fat into 2-carbon pieces, like slicing a baguette.
C-ch4-fuels.tip: Fatty acids are broken down by beta-oxidation into acetyl-CoA, which then enters the Krebs cycle.
C-ch4-fuels.why: Beta-oxidation breaks fatty acids down by removing two-carbon acetyl units, which enter the Krebs cycle as acetyl-CoA. Deamination removes the nitrogen from amino acids, glycolysis splits glucose, and glycogenolysis breaks glycogen into glucose.

C-ch4-replication.trick: Gene = one recipe in the DNA cookbook.
C-ch4-replication.tip: A gene is a DNA segment that codes for a protein or a functional RNA. It is not the whole chromosome.
C-ch4-replication.why: A gene is a DNA segment that carries the information for one functional RNA or protein. A codon is a three-base 'word' within a gene, a chromosome is one long DNA molecule carrying many genes, and the genome is all of an organism's DNA.

C-ch4-expression.trick: TRANSCRIPTION = TRANSCRIBE (copy in the same language: DNA→RNA). TRANSLATION = TRANSLATE to a new language (RNA→protein).
C-ch4-expression.tip: Transcription happens in the nucleus; translation happens at ribosomes in the cytoplasm.
C-ch4-expression.why: Transcription is making RNA from a DNA template, in the nucleus. Translation builds a polypeptide from mRNA at a ribosome, replication copies DNA into DNA, and a mutation is a change in the DNA sequence.
